spots.name: Jet d'Eau
spots.summary: The Jet d'Eau is a large fountain in Geneva, Switzerland, and is one of the city's most famous landmarks, being featured on the city's official tourism web site.

spots.name: Reformation Wall
spots.summary: The International Monument to the Reformation, usually known as the Reformation Wall, was inaugurated in 1909 in Geneva, Switzerland. Key individuals, events, and documents of the Protestant Reformation are depicted therein in statues and bas-reliefs.

spots.name: St. Pierre Cathedral
spots.summary: Saint Peter's Cathedral Geneva is a historic church in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: University of Geneva
spots.summary: The University of Geneva is a public research university located in Geneva, Switzerland. It was founded in 1559 by French theologian John Calvin as a theological seminary. It remained focused on theology until the 17th century, when it became a center for enlightenment scholarship.

spots.name: Palace of Nations
spots.summary: The Palace of Nations is the home of the United Nations Office at Geneva, located in Geneva, Switzerland. It was built between 1929 and 1938 to serve as the headquarters of the League of Nations.

spots.name: Broken Chair
spots.summary: Broken Chair is a monumental sculpture in wood designed by Swiss artist Daniel Berset, and constructed by carpenter Louis Genève. It is constructed of 5.5 tons of wood and is 12 metres high.

spots.name: Genève-Cornavin railway station
spots.summary: Geneva railway station, also known as Geneva Cornavin railway station, is Geneva's main train station, located in Cornavin area; both names can be used interchangeably.

spots.name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Musée d'art et d'histoire is an encyclopedic art museum located in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: United Nations Office at Geneva

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The United Nations Office at Geneva is one of the four major offices of the United Nations where numerous different UN agencies have a joint presence, located in Geneva.

spots.name: Brunswick Monument
spots.summary: The Brunswick Monument is a mausoleum built in 1879 in the Jardin des Alpes in Geneva, Switzerland to commemorate the life of Charles II, Duke of Brunswick (1804–1873).

spots.name: Grand Théâtre de Genève
spots.summary: Grand Théâtre de Genève is an opera house in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: Cimetière des Rois
spots.summary: The Cimetière des Rois is a cemetery in Geneva, Switzerland. The cemetery is commonly named after la rue des Rois near which it is situated. The graveyard was established in 1482 for people who died from plague in the Middle Ages, during the second plague pandemic.

spots.name: Carouge
spots.summary: Carouge is a municipality in the Canton of Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: Geneva Freeport
spots.summary: Geneva Freeport is a warehouse complex in Geneva, Switzerland, for the storage of art and other valuables and collectibles. It is the world's oldest and largest freeport facility, and the one with the most artworks, with 40% of its collection being art with an estimated value of US$100 billion.

spots.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Geneva

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Our Lady of Geneva is a Roman Catholic church and Minor Basilica located in Geneva, Switzerland. It is dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of Our Lady of Geneva

spots.name: Geneva Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Geneva Mosque, also known as the Petit-Saconnex Mosque is the largest mosque in Geneva, Switzerland. It was financed by the Saudi-based Muslim World League and constructed in 1978 in the neighborhood of Le Petit-Saconnex.

spots.name: Calvin Auditory

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Calvin Auditorium or Calvin Auditory, originally the Notre-Dame-la-Neuve Chapel, is a chapel in Geneva, Switzerland, which played a significant role in the Protestant Reformation. It is associated with John Calvin, Theodore Beza and John Knox.

spots.name: Bodmer Library

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.summary: The Bodmer Foundation is a library and museum specialised in manuscripts and precious editions. It is located in Cologny, Switzerland just outside Geneva.

spots.name: Palais Wilson

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palais Wilson in Geneva, Switzerland, is the current headquarters of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.

spots.name: Geneva Ethnography Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Musée d'ethnographie de Genève is one of the most important ethnographic museums in Switzerland.

spots.name: Pont du Mont-Blanc
spots.summary: The Pont du Mont-Blanc, sometimes anglicized as Mont Blanc Bridge, is a major bridge in Geneva. It connect the quarters of the left banks of the Rhône to those of the right banks. It is a major north–south road axis in the Canton of Geneva, since its inauguration in 1862. The bridge is about 250 metres long.

spots.name: Place du Bourg-de-Four
spots.summary: Place du Bourg-de-Four is a cobblestone square in the Old Town of Geneva, Switzerland. Located on the site of the old Roman forum and medieval market, it served as a stagecoach stop in the 19th century. It is now a popular meeting place with restaurants and cafes surrounding a small marble 18th-century fountain.

spots.name: Natural History Museum of Geneva

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Natural History Museum of Geneva is a natural history museum in Geneva, Switzerland. It is the largest natural history museum in Switzerland and one of the ten largest in Europe.

photo.author: Philippe Wagneur, Natural History Museum of Geneva (MHNG)

spots.name: Musée Ariana

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Musée Ariana, also known as the Musée suisse de la céramique et du verre, is a museum in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: L'horloge fleurie
spots.summary: L'horloge fleurie, or the flower clock, is an outdoor flower clock located on the western side of Jardin Anglais park in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: Pierres du Niton
spots.summary: The Pierres du Niton are two glacial erratics in Lake Geneva, Switzerland, in Geneva harbor. On the left bank of the lake near Quai Gustave-Ador, they are remnants from the last ice age, left by the Rhone glacier.

spots.name: Geneva Botanical Garden
spots.summary: The Geneva Botanic Garden is a botanical garden in Geneva, Switzerland. Founded in 1817 by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle, it now covers 28 hectares and holds major scientific collections, including more than 11'000 taxa in its living collections.

spots.name: Barbier-Mueller Museum
spots.summary: The Barbier-Mueller Museum, founded in 1977, is located at 10 rue Jean-Calvin, in Geneva, Switzerland. Its collection contains over 7,000 pieces and includes works of art from Tribal and Classical antiquity as well as sculptures, fabrics and ornaments from "primitive" civilizations around the world.

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

spots.name: Parc La Grange
spots.summary: The Parc La Grange is an urban park in the city of Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: Île Rousseau
spots.summary: The Île Rousseau is an island and park in Geneva, situated in the middle of the Rhone. It was named after the philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau. On the island is a statue of Rousseau.

spots.name: Musée Rath

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Musée Rath is an art museum in Geneva, used exclusively for temporary exhibitions. Its building is the oldest purpose-built art museum in Switzerland, and the original home of Geneva's Musée d'Art et d'Histoire.

spots.name: Hans Wilsdorf Bridge
spots.summary: The Hans Wilsdorf Bridge is a bridge in Geneva, Switzerland.

spots.name: International Museum of the Reformation

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The International Museum of the Reformation is a museum in Geneva, Switzerland, dedicated to the history and heritage of the Protestant Reformation. It was opened in 2005.

spots.name: Russian Church, Geneva

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Russian Church, Geneva is a historic Russian Orthodox church in Geneva, Switzerland.

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

spots.name: Victoria Hall
spots.summary: The Victoria Hall is a 1,700-seat concert venue in Geneva. It is primarily home to the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande (OSR), but also hosts performers in jazz, world music and other genres.

spots.name: Jardin Anglais
spots.summary: The Jardin anglais is an urban park in Geneva, Switzerland, situated at the location of an ancient harbor and a wood. It marks the beginning of the Quai Gustave-Ador.

spots.name: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum is a museum located in Geneva, Switzerland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum

spots.name: Immeuble Clarté
spots.summary: Immeuble Clarté is an apartment building in Geneva designed by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret starting from 1928 and built in 1931–32. It has eight stories comprising 45 free plan units of diverse configurations and sizes.

spots.name: MAMCO

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is the contemporary art museum of Geneva, which opened in 1994. The building is a former factory building, with 3500 m2 of exhibition space, it is the largest contemporary art museum of Switzerland.

spots.name: Bâtiment des Forces motrices
spots.summary: The Bâtiment des Forces motrices (BFM), French for "Power plant building", is the power house of a former hydro power plant and waterworks in Geneva called Usine des Forces Motrices, later Usine des Forces Motrices de la Coulouvrenière.

spots.name: Conservatoire de Musique
spots.summary: The Conservatoire de musique de Genève is a music school in Geneva, Switzerland.

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

spots.name: Beth Yaakov Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Beth Yaakov Synagogue, also the Great Synagogue or the Grande Synagogue, is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 11 Place de la Synagogue, Geneva, in the Canton of Geneva, Switzerland.

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

spots.name: Celestial Sphere Woodrow Wilson Memorial
spots.summary: The Celestial Sphere is an armillary sphere artpiece situated in the Palais des Nations in Geneva, Switzerland, one of the four headquarters of the United Nations. It was donated in 1939 by the Woodrow Wilson Foundation to what was then the League of Nations building.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Musée d'histoire des sciences de la Ville de Genève

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Musée d'histoire des sciences de la Ville de Genève is a small museum in Switzerland dedicated to the history of science.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Musée d'histoire des sciences de la Ville de Genève

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, Geneva, Switzerland, was completed in 1853. The church is located at rue du Mont-Blanc, between the Genève-Cornavin railway station and the famous hotels at the banks of Lake Geneva.

spots.name: Geneva Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Bibliothèque de Genève is the principal library of the City and Canton of Geneva, Switzerland. Founded in 1559, it is among the oldest libraries in the world to operate a legal deposit system, serving as the legal deposit library for the Canton of Geneva.

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

photo.author: Credits to Mourad Ben Abdallah / Wikimedia Commons

spots.name: The Contemporary African Art Collection

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Contemporary African Art Collection (CAAC) is a private collection created in 1989 by Jean Pigozzi, an Italian businessman, after his encounter with French independent curator, André Magnin. Magnin specializes in art from non-Western cultures, and especially sub-Saharan art.

spots.name: Stade de Genève
spots.summary: Stade de Genève, also called Stade de la Praille, is a stadium in Lancy, Canton of Geneva. It has a capacity of 30,084.

spots.name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Emmanuel Episcopal Church, located in Geneva, Switzerland, is an English speaking Episcopal parish of the Convocation of Episcopal Churches in Europe, and a member of the Anglican Communion.

spots.name: International Committee of the Red Cross archives
spots.summary: The archives of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) are based in Geneva and were founded in 1863 at the time of the ICRC's inception. It has the dual function to manage both current records and historical archives. The general historical archives are openly accessible to the general public up to 1975.
spots.wikipediaTitle: International Committee of the Red Cross archives

spots.name: Viaduc de la Jonction
spots.summary: The Viaduc de la Jonction is a rail viaduct in Geneva, Switzerland. It was completed in 1945.

spots.name: Old Town

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aside of the cathedral the Old town in general is worth walking around in for an hour or two. Among the highlights are the city hall with the cannons in the little square opposite to it, Rousseau's birth house and various antique shops with all sorts of interesting stuff in the windows. A word of warning to people with physical disabilities: the Old Town, is situated on a hill with quite steep str

spots.name: La Perle du Lac
spots.summary: Translates to the "Pearl of the Lake" and is the largest park on the western bank of Lake Geneva. It hosts the splendid eponymous restaurant and a free science museum, but it also a great place for a picnic.

spots.name: Genève Plage
spots.summary: There are many smaller places where to swim in either the rivers or the lake, but the largest one is Genève Plage (literally "Geneva Beach") at the eastern bank of the lake. It's a nice place to swim, enjoy the sun, play, barbecue, or just hang out.
